title: Pleroma
description: The fullness of everything: every fluid there is, poured together. Unlocks the Pleroma Confluence.

puzzle.goal: N different ideal fluids, n_i moles each, with pure-fluid chemical potentials μ_i, are poured together at temperature T. In the mixture each fluid's chemical potential gains R·T·ln of its mole fraction. Write the free energy G (at constant temperature and pressure) of the mixture minus that of the separate pure fluids, with each mole fraction written out as a ratio of sums.
puzzle.name: Gibbs energy of ideal mixing
puzzle.form: sum ( i , 1 , N , n _ i * ( μ _ i + R * T * ln ( n _ i / sum ( j , 1 , N , n _ j ) ) ) ) - sum ( i , 1 , N , n _ i * μ _ i )
puzzle.ask: With one mole of each fluid every mole fraction is 1/N, so ΔG = −N·R·T·ln N. Find ΔG (kJ) when N = @{N} different fluids are mixed at @{T} K.

vars.\u03bc: chemical potential of the pure fluid

puzzle.method: The total Gibbs energy is Σ n_i times each species' chemical potential; for an ideal mixture the potential shifts by RT ln x_i, which comes from counting the ways to arrange the molecules.
